newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: YUGOSLAVIA STAYS OUT OF EUROPEAN CHESS CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: YUGOSLAVIA STAYS OUT OF EUROPEAN CHESS CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Yugoslavia will not take part in the European chess championships in the Croatian city of Pula in May, the Yugoslav Chess Federation said on Monday.
A Federation spokesman told Belgrade's BK television station the decision not to compete was taken after consulting the federal government.
The office of Prime Minister Radoje Kontic earlier denied the government had advised the federation not to take part.

The denial came after the independent daily Nasa Borba quoted federation chairman Miodrag Vukovic as saying Kontic told the chess body the "time was still not right for any Yugoslav athletes or chess players to take part in events in Croatia."
Croatia and Yugoslavia are gradually normalising relations after fighting a war in 1991 over Croatia's secession from the Balkan federation.
Most sporting contacts since then have taken place in third countries.
